objective.statement: On HomeView the red torus widget renders under the green torus widget; it must render to the right of the green torus widget, inline.

complexity.rationale: One layout wrapper in HomeView.tsx and one component test; no state, API, dependency or TorusWidget change.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: On HomeView the green torus widget and the red torus widget sit side by side in one horizontal row, with the red widget to the right of the green widget.
The two widgets keep their DOM order (green first, red second), their colours, their 200px by 200px size and their labels; the rest of HomeView is unchanged.

in.statement: A layout wrapper around the two TorusWidget elements in HomeView.tsx, a test id for it in HomeView.testIds.ts, and a layout assertion in HomeView.component.test.tsx.

out.statement: TorusWidget internals, torus geometry, colours, labels, the other HomeView sections, theme tokens, dependencies, and historical workflow records.

observations.statement: HomeView renders <TorusWidget /> and <TorusWidget color="red" /> as direct children of the section with class space-y-6, so each widget is its own block-level row and the red one stacks under the green one.

Fix with a wrapper div using Tailwind flex row classes (flex items-start gap-4), added to HomeView only. No wrapping on narrow screens, because the card asks for inline placement. Gap of 1rem is a conservative choice matching the page's spacing scale.

jsdom does no layout, so the component test asserts the wrapper's flex row classes (flex present, flex-col absent) and that it contains the green then the red widget, via a new data-id test id. No e2e layout check is added.
